name: Angkor Lotus Boutique Hotel
nameKm: សណ្ឋាគារប៊ូទិកអង្គរឡូតាស់
shortDescription: A 24-room boutique hotel in a quiet lane off Wat Bo Road, with a saltwater pool shaded by frangipani, a Khmer restaurant and tuk-tuk drivers who know the temple circuits by heart.
description: Angkor Lotus sits in a residential lane east of the river, ten minutes on foot from the Old Market and twenty by tuk-tuk from Angkor Wat. The building is a modern take on the Khmer wooden house, with deep eaves, polished hardwood floors and open corridors around a saltwater pool. Rooms are generous for the price, with rain showers, strong air-conditioning and balconies over the garden or the pool. The restaurant serves a Khmer and continental breakfast and a short evening menu built around amok and curries. The front desk arranges temple passes, sunrise departures and licensed guides, and a small fleet of house tuk-tuk drivers handles the circuits at fixed prices. Airport transfers are free for stays of two nights or more.

name: Ta Prohm Garden Villa
nameKm: វីឡាសួនតាព្រហ្ម
shortDescription: Two private pool villas behind a high garden wall in the Wat Damnak quarter, each with its own kitchen, housekeeper and a cook who comes in for dinner on request.
description: Ta Prohm Garden Villa is a pair of private houses in a walled garden in Wat Damnak, the leafy quarter south of the river where Siem Reap's old villas stand under rain trees. Each villa has its own pool, a kitchen stocked for breakfast, a terrace for long dinners and a housekeeper who comes each morning. The smaller villa sleeps four in two bedrooms; the larger sleeps eight in four. A cook can be booked for Khmer dinners on the terrace, and a driver with a car or a tuk-tuk can be on call for temple days. The town centre is a ten-minute walk along the river. Guests are met at the airport and checked in at the house, not at a desk.

nameKm: ហូស្ទែលមាត់ស្ទឹងសៀមរាប
shortDescription: A sociable but not rowdy hostel on the east bank, with pod-style dorm beds, a rooftop terrace for sunset beers, a shared kitchen and a travel desk that books sunrise tuk-tuks.
description: Siem Reap River Hostel occupies a converted shophouse on the river road, a five-minute walk over the footbridge from Pub Street and far enough from it to sleep. Dorms are fitted with pod beds, each with a curtain, a reading light, two sockets and a locker big enough for a backpack, and there is a female-only dorm on the top floor. Four private doubles suit couples on a budget. The rooftop terrace is the heart of the place: cheap beer, a view over the river and a nightly gathering that winds down at eleven. A shared kitchen, a laundry service and a book exchange cover the basics, and the travel desk sells Angkor sunrise tuk-tuk shares, and bus and boat tickets to Battambang.

name: Kulen Hills Eco Lodge
nameKm: អេកូឡដ្ជភ្នំគូលែន
shortDescription: Twelve thatched bungalows on a forested slope below the Kulen plateau, built from local timber and run with the village next door, with guided walks to the waterfall and the river carvings.
description: Kulen Hills Eco Lodge sits at the foot of Phnom Kulen, an hour and a half north-east of Siem Reap, where the road starts to climb into the forest. Twelve bungalows of timber and thatch stand on stilts along a slope above a stream, with wide verandas, fans rather than air-conditioning, solar hot water and mosquito nets over the beds. The lodge was built with and is partly staffed by the neighbouring village, and guides from there lead walks to the waterfall, the reclining Buddha and the river of lingas. Meals are Khmer and cooked over charcoal, with vegetables from the garden. Evenings are dark, quiet and full of frogs. A pickup from Siem Reap is arranged for a fixed fee.

nameKm: ផ្ទះស្នាក់ជាមួយគ្រួសារកំពង់ភ្លុក
shortDescription: A family stilt house in Kampong Phluk with two guest rooms, meals cooked with the household, and the family's boat for the flooded forest at dawn before the day boats arrive.
description: The Chea family have lived in Kampong Phluk for four generations, and since 2015 they have taken guests into two rooms at the back of their stilt house. The rooms are simple: a mattress on a polished floor, a mosquito net, a fan when the generator runs and a shared bathroom downstairs. What you come for is the rest of it. You eat with the family, help with the fish, and go out in their boat at first light into the flooded forest. In the dry season you walk under the houses and out across the lake bed. The homestay is registered with the commune's tourism group, and part of the fee goes to the village fund. The boat from the landing is arranged when you book.

shortDescription: A 110-room riverfront hotel on Sisowath Quay with a rooftop pool, an executive lounge, a spa and a ballroom, a short walk from the Royal Palace and the National Museum.
description: Riverside Palace stands on the quay at the point where the Tonle Sap meets the Mekong, with the Royal Palace five minutes to the south. It opened in 2011 and was refurbished in 2023, and it runs as a full-service city hotel: a rooftop pool and bar over the river, an executive lounge on the top floor, a spa with Khmer treatments, a gym open round the clock, two restaurants and a ballroom that handles weddings and conferences. Rooms are large and quiet behind double glazing, most with river views, and suites add a sitting room and butler service. The concierge arranges palace and museum guides, sunset cruises from the quay below, and cars to the airport in twenty minutes.

shortDescription: A family-run guesthouse in a 1960s villa behind the Russian Market, with twelve rooms around a mango-tree garden, bicycles to borrow and the owners' own advice on where to eat.
description: BKK1 Garden Guesthouse is a two-storey 1960s villa in a side street between Boeng Keng Kang and the Russian Market, run by the Sok family since 2012. The twelve rooms are plain and clean, with tiled floors, firm beds and the choice of a fan or air-conditioning, and they open onto balconies or the garden, where two old mango trees shade the breakfast tables. Mrs Sok cooks a Khmer breakfast to order for a few dollars, and her husband keeps a list of the neighbourhood's noodle shops and cafés. Bicycles are free to borrow, tuk-tuks are called at honest prices, and laundry comes back the same day. The market is a ten-minute walk; the riverside is a short tuk-tuk ride.

description: Chaktomuk Sky Residences fills the upper fourteen floors of a tower a block back from Monivong Boulevard, opened in 2021 for people who need more than a hotel room and less than a lease. Studios and one- and two-bedroom apartments come with full kitchens, washer-dryers, fast wifi and a desk with a view, and housekeeping comes daily or weekly as you choose. The 28th floor holds an infinity pool along the river side of the building, a gym, a sauna and a lounge with meeting rooms and printing that works as a coworking space in the day. The riverside, the Central Market and the business towers are all within fifteen minutes on foot, and the front desk arranges airport cars, SIM cards and visa extensions.

shortDescription: A weaving family's compound on Koh Dach with three guest rooms and a riverside bungalow, hand looms under the house, bicycles for the island lanes and dinner cooked on the riverbank.
description: Silk Island River Lodge is the home and workshop of the Rath family, who have woven silk on Koh Dach for generations. Three rooms upstairs in the wooden house and a bungalow by the water take guests, and the looms clack under the house from early morning. Guests can sit at a loom with a weaver, dye thread in the yard, or simply take a bicycle and ride the island's lanes to the temples and the dry-season beach at the northern tip. Meals are cooked by the family and eaten on a platform over the Mekong. Phnom Penh is within reach for a day and a world away at night, when the only sound is the river and the generator at the temple down the lane.

shortDescription: Fourteen bungalows set among the pepper rows of a working farm near Damnak Kantuot, with a spring-fed pool, farm tours every morning and dinners built around the estate's own pepper.
description: Kampot Pepper Estate Bungalows sits on a six-hectare working pepper farm twenty-five minutes east of Kampot town, in the red-earth country between the Secret Lake and the Kep hills. The bungalows are brick and timber with tiled roofs, spaced along the edge of the pepper rows so that the view from every veranda is a wall of green vines on their poles. A spring-fed pool sits under the mango trees, and the open restaurant serves Khmer dishes that show off the farm's four colours of pepper. Guests join the farm walk each morning and help with sorting in harvest season. Bicycles and a map cover the lake, the cave at Phnom Chhnork and the salt fields; a shuttle runs to Kampot and Kep twice a day.

shortDescription: A friendly riverside guesthouse on the Kampot waterfront with fourteen rooms, a rooftop that faces Bokor at sunset, motorbikes to rent and a desk that sorts out the boat trips.
description: Bokor View is a three-storey guesthouse on the river road north of the Old Bridge, run by a Kampot family who opened it in 2010. The rooms are simple and well kept, with tiled floors, hot showers and a choice of fan or air-conditioning; the ones at the front have balconies over the river, and all guests share the rooftop terrace, where the Bokor ridge turns pink at six and everyone drinks a beer. Downstairs a small café does eggs, baguettes and Khmer noodle soup for breakfast. The desk rents motorbikes and bicycles, books the sunset and firefly boats that leave from the quay outside, and arranges shared taxis to the pepper farms, Kep and the Bokor road. Buses to Phnom Penh stop two streets away.

shortDescription: Two private villas on the Kep shoreline with pools that look over the gulf to Rabbit Island, a chef who shops at the crab market each morning, and a boat for the islands.
description: Kep Seaside Villa is a pair of modern houses on a lawn that runs down to the rocks west of the crab market, each with a long pool facing the Gulf of Thailand and the low shape of Rabbit Island on the horizon. The three-bedroom villa suits a family; the five-bedroom one, on two floors with a roof deck, takes two families or a group of friends. Both come with a housekeeper, a night guard and a chef who goes to the crab market at seven and cooks whatever is best that day, from pepper crab to grilled squid. The villa's boat runs to Rabbit Island and the mangroves on request, kayaks and bicycles are in the garage. Kep town is five minutes by tuk-tuk.

shortDescription: A beachfront resort at the quiet southern end of Otres with 48 rooms and villas, a spa under the casuarinas, two pools, kayaks and paddleboards, and a restaurant on the sand.
description: Otres Beach Resort & Spa occupies two hundred metres of beachfront at the far end of Otres, where the casuarinas close in and the hills of Ream begin. It opened in 2013 and has stayed low: two-storey garden wings, a row of beachfront villas with private plunge pools, and a main pool and a quieter adults-only pool beneath the trees. The spa works in open pavilions with Khmer herbal compresses and sea-salt scrubs, the water-sports hut lends kayaks and paddleboards, and the beach restaurant does a long seafood lunch and a candlelit dinner on the sand. Rooms are cool and simple, with timber, white linen and outdoor showers. Sihanoukville's ferry pier is twenty minutes away, the airport fifteen, and the resort shuttle covers both.

shortDescription: Sixteen wooden bungalows on the west coast of Koh Rong, facing the sunset over Sok San beach, with a restaurant on the sand, kayaks, snorkel gear and a boat from Koh Touch three times a day.
description: Koh Rong Sunset Bungalows stands on the long western beach of Koh Rong, a thirty-minute boat ride from the pier at Koh Touch and a world away from its bars. Sixteen bungalows of local timber are set back among the trees, some on the sand and some on the slope behind, with fans, nets and solar hot water; electricity comes from the resort's own system and runs around the clock. The restaurant sits on the beach and does grilled fish from the village boats, and Khmer curries, and its tables are the place to be when the sun goes down into the sea. Kayaks and snorkel gear are free, boat trips go to the reefs and to the plankton after dark, and the staff know the island's paths.

shortDescription: A barefoot hostel on the west coast of Koh Rong Sanloem with two dorms, six beach huts, a kitchen for guests, hammocks in the trees and nothing to do after dark but watch the plankton.
description: Sanloem Lazy Beach Hostel sits at the end of the jungle path from Saracen Bay, on the quiet western shore where the sun sets into the sea. It is deliberately simple: a twelve-bed dorm and an eight-bed dorm in a wooden longhouse, six thatched huts on the sand for couples, a shared kitchen, a small bar with cold beer and a shelf of swapped books. Power runs from solar panels and a generator in the evening, there is no air-conditioning and the wifi is a rumour, which is the point. Days go to the beach, and the snorkelling off the rocks; nights go to the hammocks and the glowing water. The hostel's longtail boat meets the ferries at Saracen Bay for those who would rather not walk the path.

shortDescription: A restored 1920s shophouse on the riverside with nine high-ceilinged rooms, original floor tiles, a courtyard café and bicycles for the galleries and the countryside beyond.
description: Battambang Colonial House is a corner shophouse from the 1920s on the river road, restored over two years by the family who still run it. The nine rooms keep the bones of the building: four-metre ceilings, patterned floor tiles, teak shutters and the long balcony that runs along the first floor over the street. The ground floor is a café open to the courtyard, where the coffee comes from a Battambang roaster. The owners know the art quarter well and keep a hand-drawn map of galleries, studios and the circus schedule at the desk. Bicycles are free, and a day's ride takes in the bamboo train, the temples at Banan and the bat cave at Phnom Sampeau. Boats to Siem Reap leave from the pier two blocks north.

description: Sen Monorom Hill Lodge is spread across a grassy hillside a kilometre above the town, where the Mondulkiri plateau rolls away in green folds to the horizon. The bungalows are clad in local pine with tin roofs that drum in the rain, each with a veranda facing the valley, a proper duvet for the cool nights and a hot shower that matters at this altitude. The restaurant has a fireplace that is lit from December to February and a menu that leans on Bunong recipes, highland coffee and vegetables from the lodge's garden. Guides from the Bunong village down the hill lead walks to waterfalls and through the forest, and the lodge shuttle runs to Bou Sra, the elephant sanctuary and the coffee farms.

shortDescription: A plain, well-run 30-room hotel on the Kratie riverfront, with Mekong views from the upper floors, a breakfast terrace, bicycles for Koh Trong and a desk that books the dolphin boats and the buses.
description: Kratie Mekong View is a four-storey hotel on the riverfront road, facing the ferry landing for Koh Trong and the long sunsets over the island. It has been running since 2008 and has recently redone its bathrooms and its wifi, but the character is unchanged: tiled rooms, firm beds, cold air-conditioning, and a staff who will book anything in the province at the price the locals pay. The upper floors look over the Mekong; the lower ones over the market behind. Breakfast is served on a terrace at the front with the river traffic going by. shortDescription: Ten bungalows and rooms in a garden near Banlung's market, run by a Tampuan family, with motorbikes for the red roads, trekking arranged with the park office and a short ride to Yeak Laom.
description: Banlung Lake Guesthouse is a cluster of wooden bungalows and a two-storey block set in a garden of jackfruit and cashew trees on the east side of Banlung, a ten-minute motorbike ride from the crater lake and five from the market. The owners are Tampuan, and the guesthouse has become the easy way into Ratanakiri: they rent motorbikes with a map of the waterfalls, gem mines and villages, arrange boats on the Sesan, and book treks into Virachey through the park office with guides they know. Rooms are simple and clean with fans or air-conditioning and hot showers, and the bungalows have hammocks on the veranda. Breakfast is eggs, fruit, baguettes and strong Ratanakiri coffee under the trees. Evenings in the garden are quiet apart from the geckos.

shortDescription: Ten floating and bank-side bungalows on the Tatai river at the edge of the Cardamoms, reached by boat, with kayaks, guided forest walks, a candlelit restaurant and the waterfall twenty minutes upstream.
description: Tatai River Ecolodge sits on a bend of the Tatai where the mangroves give way to rainforest, twenty minutes by boat from the bridge on National Road 48 and twenty more from the waterfall. Six bungalows float on pontoons along the bank and four stand on the slope behind, all built of timber and thatch with solar power, composting toilets and wide decks over the water. The day is kayaking, swimming off the deck, a guided walk into the forest with a ranger from the village, and the boat to the falls. The restaurant is on a floating platform, lit by candles and run on what the village fishermen and farmers bring in. The lodge employs mostly from Tatai village and pays into its forest fund.
